The listed nonzero values give
\[
\gcd(126,2184,16380,-126)=42.
\]
Now \(42=2\cdot 3\cdot 7\). For every integer \(n\):
- mod \(2\): \(n^7\equiv n\).
- mod \(3\): if \(3\mid n\), trivial; otherwise \(n^2\equiv1\), so \(n^6\equiv1\), hence \(n^7\equiv n\).
- mod \(7\): if \(7\mid n\), trivial; otherwise by Fermat \(n^6\equiv1\), so \(n^7\equiv n\).

Thus \(42\mid n^7-n\) for all \(n\). Since the common divisor cannot exceed
\[
\gcd(2^7-2,3^7-3)=\gcd(126,2184)=42,
\]
the GCD is \(\boxed{42}\).
